items.description: Disassembly and disposal of damaged floor tiles in bathroom
items.rationale: Covered as necessary preparatory work for repair of water-damaged floor (7.1.7(a), 2.4.2). Scope matches affected area. Reference cases 50, 56, 46 show t per m² between 40 and 50; for 6 m², t ≈ 270.

items.description: New installation of floor tiles in bathroom incl. material
items.rationale: Repair of water-damaged floor to pre-loss standard is covered (7.1.1(b), 7.1.7(c), 2.4.2). Reference cases 56, 50: supply & lay tiles 8 m² t ≈ 877, 5 m² t ≈ 433; for 6 m², interpolate t ≈ 650.
General cleaning of unaffected areas is not a repair cost (7.1.8(a)); only cleaning of directly affected surfaces is covered. No evidence whole apartment was affected.

items.description: Paint lower wall after water damage incl. surface preparation
items.rationale: Painting water-stained lower wall (20 m²) is repair of affected area (7.1.1(b), 7.1.5). Reference: painting disturbed wall area t ≈ 633–650 per wall, but here 20 m² is a large area; estimate t ≈ 650.
Ceiling was not affected by water (description: 'looked completely fine'); work beyond affected parts is excluded (7.1.5).
Hallway was not affected by water (description: 'nothing there either'); work beyond affected parts is excluded (7.1.5).

items.description: Remove water-damaged laminate in living room
items.rationale: Removal of water-damaged laminate is necessary preparatory work (7.1.7(a), 2.4.2). Reference: removal of skirting/laminate t ≈ 80–93 per 10 m, so for 18 m², t ≈ 150.

items.description: Supply & install laminate incl. impact sound insulation
items.rationale: Replacement of water-damaged laminate to pre-loss standard is covered (7.1.1(b), 7.1.7(c)). Reference: supply & lay tiles 8 m² t ≈ 877, so for 18 m² laminate (cheaper than tile), t ≈ 1400.
Skirting along affected wall (25 m) was water-damaged. Reference: replace skirting boards t per m ≈ 124 (case 59), so for 25 m, t ≈ 3100.
